text:
Some historical items like pioneer relics and moveable objects, could be removed and saved; however, the site itself will be lost.
It is not possible to predict with certainty how the culture and way of life of the Crow Indians will respond to social and economic effects of Tract II and Tract III coal extraction. It is likely that any such changes would be irreversible.
If a coal conversion facility were to be constructed, irretrievable commitments of natural and human resources would increase proportionately. Agricultural production and wildlife values on the plant site, and certain aesthetic values would be foregone for the life of the facility. An estimated 16,000 acre feet of water per year for process and cooling would be irretrievably committed. Introduction of trace elements to terrestrial ecosystems via atmospheric fallout would be irreversible.
